$comment: AGENTS.md 2.3: every @Public use is listed here with its justification, so exemptions are reviewable rather than invisible. check-route-guards.mjs fails when the decorator and this file disagree in EITHER direction - a route with no entry, or an entry whose route no longer exists. An unreconciled allowlist decays into a historical document and stops constraining anything.

routes.reason: Starts a Google OIDC sign-in. It is the only route a browser can reach before a session exists, so a permission check here would require the permission the route exists to obtain. It grants nothing and changes nothing: no session, no row, no school data, no role consulted. Hence no @RequireEntitlement, and no @Audited - the audit record belongs on GET /auth/oidc/callback, where a stranger's assertion becomes a local account. AGENTS.md 2.3 and 2.13.

The one-time setup token IS the credential on this route. A permission check would require the permission the route exists to grant: no account, session or role exists before the token is spent, and the deployment state it reads is precisely what a permission system cannot gate. It is the only UNAUTHENTICATED WRITE in the system, and it is bounded by three things that are all independent of RBAC: the token itself (256 bits of CSPRNG, stored only as SHA-256, single-use, inside one transaction with the credential write), argon2id (so a guess costs tens of milliseconds and 19 MiB), and a per-source throttle that answers 429. @Audited('SETUP_COMPLETE') is present as the AGENTS.md 2.3 vocabulary requires, and PLT-402 is the story that will write the row - nothing reads that metadata today. AGENTS.md 2.3, 2.13, 2.14.

Sign-in is how a session is obtained, so a permission check would require the permission the route exists to grant - the same circularity as the OIDC redirect, and the reason D57 makes this route MANDATORY rather than a fallback: Google must-link, so a session is the only way anything can be linked. Unlike the redirect this route does change state, because it issues a session; what makes the exemption safe is scope rather than inertness - it acts only on the caller, only on a credential they presented, and only when that credential verifies. No other account is read or written, no role is consulted, no school data is reachable. No @RequireEntitlement, because a Basic-edition school must still be able to sign in or it cannot use the product at all. @Audited('LOGIN') is present per AGENTS.md 2.3 and will cover both success and failure; PLT-402 will write the rows, and the constraint recorded in the controller is that a failure record must carry no identifier and no credential, or the audit log becomes the enumeration oracle the route exists to prevent. AGENTS.md 2.3, 2.13.
